    {"id":"Q001","answer":"An Exile who takes Oathkeeper during Act cannot win as Usurper in that same turn. At the next Wake, they are checked while still Oathkeeper, then flip the title to Usurper; the first Usurper victory check is at their following Wake, unless round 8 ends first while they still hold Usurper. If someone takes the title away before that check, they cannot win as Usurper; retaking it resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.","support":"supported","evidence":"Victory checked before the flip; win at following Wake or round-8 end; losing title prevents the win; retaking resets sequence (Victory)."},
    {"id":"Q002","answer":"Supremacy matches Conquest; Protection matches Rebellion; Sanctuary matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win also requires an Exile to have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player; a tie does not count.","support":"supported","evidence":"Oath/goal table and Visionary victory paragraphs (Victory)."},
    {"id":"Q003","answer":"At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7.     {"id":"Q004","answer":"At the end of round 8, check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins—Chancellor unless a Citizen qualifies for Successor; (2) otherwise, Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise, qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous Vision priority Conquest, then Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again Chancellor unless a Citizen qualifies for Successor, even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.","support":"supported","evidence":"‘War exhaustion’ enumerates all four priority steps and simultaneous Vision order (Victory)."},
    {"id":"Q005","answer":"Successor goals by Oath: Supremacy—rule most sites; Protection—hold the most relics and banners combined; Sanctuary—hold People's Favor; Devotion—hold Darkest Secret. A Citizen cannot win by a true Vision or by becoming Usurper.","support":"supported","evidence":"Successor table; ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper’ (Victory)."},
    {"id":"Q006","answer":"At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose either to put 1 favor from your board onto the banner or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied least-full banks). You cannot remove its last favor: if it has 1, add 1 if able; if you have none, do nothing. On Mob side, repeat that choice once. After the choice(s), check whether it has at least 6 favor and flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this final check does not make you repeat the payment during that Wake.","support":"supported","evidence":"Wake step 1 states choices, last-favor restriction, repeat on Mob side, then threshold flip (Wake)."},
    {"id":"Q007","answer":"Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip your facedown board secrets faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Exile/Chancellor according to warbands left in personal bank, while a Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost; (4) move the Supply marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); (5) optionally use each Rest power once, in chosen order. Chancellor refresh is 6 at 18+, 5 at 11–17, 4 at 4–10, 3 at 0–3; Exile is 6 at 9+, 5 at 4–8, 4 at 0–3. Saved unspent Supply thus increases next Supply by shifting the marker left, subject to the cap.","support":"supported","evidence":"Rest mandatory order and refresh bands in Turn Structure; saved Supply step."},
    {"id":"Q008","answer":"Search chooses either the world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret changes the world-deck cost to 2, with other applicable modifiers still applying. Draw up to 3, stopping early only for source exhaustion, a world-deck Vision, or a draw modifier. Drawing a world-deck Vision requires announcing that a Vision was drawn (not necessarily its identity), immediately stopping and advancing Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile neither stops Search nor advances that track.","support":"supported","evidence":"Search costs and draw procedure (Actions → Search)."},
    {"id":"Q009","answer":"Discarded cards go facedown atop the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle, with multiple discards ordered as you choose. A hand/adviser discard uses the pile after your pawn's region; never your current region's pile. When discarding a card from a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region instead. Favor on discarded cards immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.","support":"supported","evidence":"‘Discard destinations’ specifies regional cycle and resources on discarded cards (Search)."},
    {"id":"Q010","answer":"You may have at most 3 advisers, counting both faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser as permitted by its state and locks; if an incoming card changes the limit, check the new limit before playing it (use the lowest of multiple limits). A facedown adviser can be played faceup legally or discarded later as a minor action, and may be peeked at; while facedown it has no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card—including site-only cards and Visions—may be held that way. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will; it leaves only when a rule permits/requires it, respecting locks. An Exile may reveal/play a true Vision from a facedown adviser as a minor action into the separate Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding the old revealed Vision; it is not an adviser. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.","support":"supported","evidence":"Adviser rules in Search and Minor actions; true Vision handling in Search (Actions)."},
    {"id":"Q011","answer":"Muster costs 1 Supply: at your pawn's site, place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets already), then gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; Citizens take purple. A relic or ruin is ineligible, and site rule is unnecessary. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. For the first mode, put 1 secret on it and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. For the second, put 2 favor on it and gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank; with no matching advisers this yields zero secrets, though the 2 favor cost is still paid. Facedown advisers do not match. Limited favor/warbands yield only what is available; secrets are unlimited.","support":"supported","evidence":"Muster and Trade action entries give eligibility, payment, and gains (Actions)."},
    {"id":"Q012","answer":"Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target's cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay the printed site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then put it faceup in your personal bank. You cannot Recover player-held or Reliquary relics. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds, add the payment to the banner, then distribute its old favor one at a time among suit banks, starting at any chosen bank and proceeding away from the world deck in printed order, wrapping as needed; do not return old favor to the prior holder, and flip Mob to normal. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds and add them; new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from shared bank, the remainder stays there. Banner seizure penalty does not apply to Recover.","support":"supported","evidence":"Recover action and its two banner procedures (Actions → Recover)."},
    {"id":"Q013","answer":"Another player's Darkest Secret is recoverable only if at least one suited card at that player's pawn site has a suit matching none of that player's faceup advisers. One such mismatch is enough even if other site cards match. If they have no faceup advisers but there is a suited card at the site, it is recoverable. Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect the banner because they have no suited card; ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. This protection does not apply when recovering from yourself or the shared bank.","support":"supported","evidence":"Corrected Darkest Secret protection paragraph (Recover)."},
    {"id":"Q014","answer":"Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender; if no player rules your site, bandits may be chosen. At least one target must be at your pawn's site, and if defender rules that site you must target it. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map, one defense die per site. If defender's pawn is at your site, you may additionally target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to banner resources), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic can itself satisfy the local-target requirement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Campaign steps 1–2 specify defender eligibility and local/remote targets (Campaign)."},
    {"id":"Q015","answer":"Attacker chooses up to one attack die per warband in the attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers. Defense is shields rolled (each double-symbol doubles shields, with multipliers stacking), plus defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender board force if the defender pawn is at the attacker site or any targeted site; doubles do not multiply warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count each full sword; each pair of hollow swords adds one attack, with a lone hollow sword counting zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never more. Attack must strictly exceed defense; tie or lower is defender victory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Campaign steps 2, 4 and 5 (Campaign)."},
    {"id":"Q016","answer":"On attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; zero placement leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. For each seized banner taken by any means other than Recover, burn 2 banner resources down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and may independently burn half the defender's board favor rounded down. Respect site travel restrictions, with enemy-ruled Shrouded Wood choosing the destination if its power applies. Then resolve attacker's victorious battle-plan effects and discard plans marked ‘At end, discard.’","support":"supported","evidence":"Campaign steps 6–8 give ordered defeat, target, and plan resolution."},
    {"id":"Q017","answer":"When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender permission if their pawn is at attacker site or a targeted site. The defending side activates all modifiers ruled by defender/Allies and shares powers as one side; allied board warbands contribute only when that Ally's pawn is at attacker site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies can use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; each shared plan is usable once total by one user, who pays. The declared defender chooses order, timing, priority, and which Ally uses a shared plan. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizens' board warbands remain there. The Oathkeeper defense bonus is shared even outside Supremacy. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. Other Citizens do not all lose Imperial status in an intra-Empire Campaign.","support":"supported","evidence":"Campaign step 1 and ‘Imperial defense’ rules (Campaign)."},
    {"id":"Q018","answer":"Base Travel costs by origin/destination region are: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, any region 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Reveal a facedown destination, place its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and its printed relics facedown from relic deck. Apply the fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. A power saying spend no Supply is the final override and makes payment zero despite another increase, including on banishment. Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by a specific power. Costs shown are the base costs before modifiers.","support":"supported","evidence":"Travel table and cost order paragraph (Travel)."},
    {"id":"Q019","answer":"In play, the Grand Scepter holder (including an Exile) may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use the offer power on the turn they took the Scepter. A later offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the recipient flips to Citizen and replaces all their board/map warbands with purple; if purple is insufficient, they choose which warbands to remove and replace. They discard revealed Vision, flip their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end their Act if accepting during their turn, and refresh Supply to full leftmost. They exchange promised pieces, and Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. No other immediate transfer is implied beyond promised exchanges.","support":"supported","evidence":"Citizenship during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, and Acceptance sections."},
    {"id":"Q020","answer":"Chronicle Oath: a win by Vision alone selects the matching next Oath; any other or multiple victory methods let the winner choose any Oath except the current one. For Chronicle Citizenship, if the winner is an Exile, first flip all Citizen boards, including boxed boards, to Exile; then the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. This Chronicle offer needs no Reliquary relic, resource payment, or Scepter permission, and the winner cannot offer themself. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle all denizens remaining in play (excluding those retained at sites, Archive, or Dispossessed), then make a top stack of 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards), a middle stack of 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), and remaining denizens below. The Chronicle aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect; it would make 14, so use 10 + 2.","support":"supported","evidence":"‘Vow an Oath,’ ‘Free Chronicle Citizenship,’ and ‘Rebuild world deck’ (Writing the Chronicle)."}
